title: 1.0.25: test addresses one keystroke away
body: Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux) and type “test” for twelve real XRP Ledger accounts to try the app with: well-known issuers, a multi-signature account, an escrow wallet, an AMM pool, an unfunded address and a Testnet account. Picking one opens the screen where it shows something, already filled in. The app also takes on the new blue lotus mark and palette.

title: 1.0.24: addresses you paste into the invoice check just work
body: The receiving account and issuer fields ignore the spaces and invisible characters copying can add, and no longer get capitalised or autocorrected. A mistyped address is caught by its checksum before the ledger is read, with a plain message instead of a destination mismatch. X-addresses are accepted and split into the account and its tag.

title: 1.0.23: did this transaction pay this invoice?
body: A new Invoice check panel on the Settlement screen reads the transaction from the XRP Ledger and answers VERIFIED, HOLD or REJECTED, with the reason. It credits only what was delivered, so a partial payment that fell short is rejected; it compares amounts exactly and reads from two independent operators by default. The same check is available to integrations through the Compliance API, with signed evidence.

title: 1.0.22: support can look at your app and fix it, only when you allow it
body: When support asks to look, the app asks you on whatever screen you are on: 4, 24 or 72 hours, and whether fixes may run without asking. Support sees a read-only snapshot of one computer (version, ledger connection, clock, sign-in, plan, settings health, recent errors; never keys or addresses) and sends fixes from a fixed list to that computer only. Every request is in the ticket's log.

title: 1.0.21: large issuers load, plainer screens
body: Issuer screens no longer fail on large issuers such as Bitstamp: when a public server cannot return the total supply in time, the survey shows the holders it read and says so. The welcome screen and Overview open with three live cards, and the website homepage goes from 23 sections to 8.

title: Book health: quoted versus funded depth on the main XRP books, live
body: A free page that reads the Bitstamp, GateHub, RLUSD and SOLO books from validated ledgers and shows how much of the advertised depth is actually funded, today and at each of the last seven daily closes. Nothing is stored; every day is re-read at the ledger index shown.

title: Product brief: the problems NOSHASHI solves, how it earns, every feature
body: One page with the XRP Ledger problems the product addresses, the plans and prices checkout charges, every screen and paid feature in the build, and what is not built yet. A test keeps it in step with the app and the billing catalogue.

title: Treasury report for companies that hold XRP
body: Holdings, reserves and who can move each wallet at a period end, and how much of the holding funded dollar offers could absorb. Read from validated ledgers with a SHA-256 digest; prints to PDF.

title: 1.0.20: annual prices, coming-soon items marked, a stricter website
body: Enterprise and Strategic are priced by the year; the uptime SLA, single sign-on and dedicated environments are marked coming soon. The website runs no inline script. An internal security assessment ran on 30 September, and SOC 2 readiness documents and contract templates were added.

title: 1.0.15: real domain and credential registry, audit evidence, readable at any size
body: Every permissioned domain and credential on mainnet, read by a sweep of the ledger; admission checks with SHA-256 records; audit trails screened against OFAC and the scam registry with a signed manifest. Text is larger, scaling fills the window, and 2FA sign-in is fixed.

title: 1.0.14: safer to hold XRP, easier to trust who holds it
body: An emergency kit for drained accounts, a reviewed scam registry and phishing check, withdrawal screening, and Customer Asset Protection: proof from the XRP Ledger that customer XRP is backed and yours is counted. Verification, not insurance.

title: Every download is now labelled BETA
body: The desktop builds are pre-1.0 and unsigned while the release pipeline is hardened. The download section now says so on every artifact rather than only in the operator note underneath, so the channel is never read as stable by accident.

title: Public site rebuilt around live feeds
body: The site now carries a live XRP newsroom, this mission log, a support console and a contact channel. Every page is rendered on the server before it is served, so the content is in the HTML a crawler receives rather than assembled afterwards in the browser.

title: Accounts and the hosted workspace were withdrawn from the site
body: Sign-in and the hosted dashboard are gone. NOSHASHI runs on your machine and reads public ledger state; the website no longer asks anyone to create an account to evaluate it. Existing links redirect rather than breaking.
